name: Levothyroxine
executiveSummary: T4 hormone. Adult hypothyroidism: start **25–50 µg PO/day** (elderly/cardiac **12.5–25 µg**); usual maintenance **75–150 µg/day**. Pediatrics: **10–15 µg/kg/day** in neonates; then by age/weight. IV myxedema: load **200–400 µg** (specialist).
indications:
## Indications

- Primary/central hypothyroidism; goiter; TSH suppression in differentiated thyroid cancer (regimens).
- Myxedema coma (IV + support).

## Precautions

- Take fasting, 30–60 min before breakfast; separate from calcium/iron/PPI ~4 h.
- Do not start high doses in ischemic heart disease.
- Adjust by TSH/free T4 (6–8 weeks after change).
- Brands not always bioequivalent — avoid unnecessary switches.

> Overdose: iatrogenic thyrotoxicosis.

adulto.dose: Young euthyroid start: **50–100 µg PO/day**. >50 y / CV: **12.5–25 µg/day**, ↑ every 3–6 weeks. Typical maintenance **1.6 µg/kg/day** (~**75–150 µg**). Myxedema IV: load **200–400 µg** then **50–100 µg/day** IV/PO — ICU.
adulto.administration: PO fasting with water. Slow IV in hospital.

pediatrico.administration: PO; crush in water/breast milk if needed (not with soy/calcium).

neonatal.dose: Congenital hypothyroidism: **10–15 µg/kg/day** PO (target high-normal free T4, falling TSH).

stability:
## Stability

- Protect from moisture/light; avoid prolonged storage in humid pillboxes.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

From excess: palpitations, nervousness, insomnia, weight loss, osteoporosis (chronic), arrhythmia. Rare excipient allergy.
